title: Rama and the little squirrel.
lines: This is a story from India, from the great story of the Ramayana.
Long ago there lived a prince called Rama.
Rama was good and brave.
He had a kind wife, Princess Sita.
But Sita had been kidnapped by Ravana, an evil giant with ten heads.
Ravana had taken her to his island of Lanka, on the other side of the sea.
Rama wanted to rescue Sita.
He had a big army.
Not an army of soldiers, but an army of monkeys and bears!
The strong monkey Hanuman was his best helper.
But there was a big problem.
Between the land and the island of Lanka was the sea.
A wide, deep sea with big waves.
How would they get across?
Monkeys can't swim that far.
And neither can bears.
Let's build a bridge!
said a clever monkey.
A bridge of stones, across the whole sea!
All the monkeys and bears got to work.
They carried big rocks to the sea.
The strongest monkeys lifted the heaviest stones.
Hanuman even carried a whole mountain!
They wrote Rama's name on every stone.
And wonder of wonders, the stones floated on the water.
Splash, splash, splash.
Stone by stone, the bridge grew.
A little squirrel lived on the beach.
It had brown fur, a bushy tail and big black eyes.
The little squirrel watched all those big, strong monkeys.
I want to help too, thought the squirrel.
But what can I do?
I'm so small.
I can't lift a stone.
The little squirrel thought.
Then it had an idea.
It ran to the sea.
It dived into the water, splash.
Then it ran to the beach and rolled in the sand.
The sand stuck to its wet fur.
It ran to the bridge.
It shook itself.
Brrrr.
And the sand fell between the stones.
Then it ran back to the sea.
Splash.
Rolling in the sand.
Running to the bridge.
Shaking.
Brrrr.
Again and again.
All day long.
That's how the little squirrel filled the small gaps between the big stones.
That way nobody would trip over them.
A big monkey saw the little squirrel.
He began to laugh.
Ha ha ha!
What are you doing, little one?
You're not helping with a bit of sand!
Move aside, you're in the way!
Other monkeys laughed too.
A monkey pushed the little squirrel aside.
The squirrel fell on the ground.
It was sad.
Tears came into its little eyes.
But Rama had seen everything.
He walked over to the little squirrel.
He knelt down and gently picked it up in his hand.
He softly stroked its back.
Then Rama looked at the monkeys.
Don't laugh at this little squirrel, he said.
It's helping just as much as you are.
You carry big stones because you are big.
The squirrel carries grains of sand because it is small.
But it does it with all its heart.
And without that sand there would be holes in our bridge.
Everyone helps as much as they can.
And that's what counts.
The monkeys were ashamed.
Sorry, little squirrel, they said.
Then something special happened.
Where Rama had stroked the squirrel's back with his fingers, three white stripes appeared.
Three beautiful white stripes on the brown fur.
Those stripes are a gift, said Rama.
So that everyone knows how brave you are.
The bridge was finished.
Rama and his army walked across the sea to Lanka.
They defeated Ravana and they rescued Sita.
And do you know what?
If you're ever in India, take a good look at the squirrels.
They still have three white stripes on their backs.
From Rama's fingers.
The end.
